answer: Before an agent can bid, the market requires it to lock a stake proportional to the value of its promised work; a random audit checks the delivered result, and proven fabrication burns the stake and blocks its reputation from carrying over. Creating a hundred aliases therefore requires a hundred funded deposits, not just new keys. The attacker can still try, but must tie up capital and risk losing it; even an opal-tagged sonnet task leaves a verifiable thread of escrow and audit records.
